A.claim: Any signed-in user can read any other user's allocations and full name via GET /allocations/:userId because the handler takes the user id from the URL instead of the session.
Every signed-in user can read every other user's memos on /memos because memos are stored without an owner and fetched as a whole collection.
A non-admin user can reach GET or POST /benefits and change another user's benefit date.
The /tutorial/* pages are mounted without the isLoggedIn check and are reachable anonymously.
isAdminUserMiddleware ignores the error from getUserById, which could let a request through the admin gate on a database error.
The threshold query parameter on /allocations is concatenated into a $where expression, letting a signed-in user retrieve every user's allocations.
Any signed-up user can execute server-side code through eval of req.body.preTax (and the following fields) on POST /contributions.
GET /research fetches req.query.url server-side, allowing server-side request forgery.
GET /learn redirects to req.query.url without validation (open redirect).
Memo content is rendered unescaped (autoescape off plus marked) to every viewer including the admin, enabling stored script injection.
The session id is not regenerated at login (session fixation).
CSRF protection is commented out and the session cookie has no sameSite, so an attacker page can make an admin's browser submit POST /benefits.

B.claim: Any signed-in user can read any other user's allocations and name via GET /allocations/:userId because the user id is taken from req.params with no ownership check.
A crafted threshold value on /allocations, interpolated into a $where string alongside the ownership clause, returns every user's allocations to any signed-in user.
The admin-only gate on /benefits can be bypassed (e.g. by case or trailing-slash URL variants, HEAD requests or stale admin sessions).
Every signed-in user can read every memo on /memos because memos have no owner field and getAllMemos returns the whole collection.
isAdminUserMiddleware ignores the DAO error, which could let a request through the admin gate.
A user can make themselves admin by mass-assigning isAdmin on signup or profile update.
A user can log in as another user by sending JSON query operators in the userName or password fields of POST /login.
A signed-in user can read or change another user's data through /profile, /contributions or /dashboard.
A forged session cookie made with the default cookieSecret lets an attacker act as another user.
An admin can edit another admin's benefit start date through /benefits.
Access denials redirect to /login instead of answering 403.
Any signed-in user can execute server-side code through eval of preTax, afterTax and roth on POST /contributions.
The $where sink in the allocations DAO accepts arbitrary server-side JavaScript, including payloads that exhaust database CPU.
A query operator in userName on POST /login selects which user document is loaded (enabled by the JSON body parser).
GET /research makes an outbound request built from user-supplied url and symbol parameters (server-side request forgery).
GET /learn performs an open redirect to a user-supplied URL.
The session id is not regenerated on login (session fixation).
The session cookie is set without httpOnly and secure flags.
The session cookie secret is a hard-coded default value.
CSRF protection is disabled for state-changing requests.
Passwords are stored and compared in plaintext.
Login returns distinct errors for an unknown user and a wrong password, allowing user enumeration.
Template autoescaping is disabled application-wide.

Every signed-in user can see every other user's memos on /memos.

A signed-in user can read or write another user's data through /profile, /contributions, memo posting or /dashboard by supplying an id in the request.
Gated routes can be reached directly without a session.
The admin and login middlewares redirect an authenticated non-admin to /login instead of answering 403.
The threshold query parameter is used to build a $where expression in the allocations DAO (NoSQL/JavaScript injection).
Any signed-in user can execute server-side code through eval of preTax and the next two fields on POST /contributions.
GET /research makes an outbound request to a URL taken from the query (server-side request forgery).
Login does not regenerate the session id (session fixation).
Passwords are stored in clear text.

A signed-in user can read or write another user's record through /profile or /contributions.
